records.name: ProtAgents
records.demonstrated_target: PDB and de novo proteins; coarse-grained protein elastic networks
records.boundary_conditions: Finite protein structures represented by anisotropic spring networks; no periodic-cell example is inferred

sources.locator: Results §2.1–2.3 and Fig.3; Materials and Methods, Natural vibrational frequency calculations
sources.evidence_paraphrase: GPT-4 agents plan and invoke protein generation/folding and physics calculations; examples execute ProDy anisotropic-network normal-mode calculations on retrieved and generated structures. Chroma and OmegaFold generate the protein geometries.
The primary submission record dates the first version to 27 January 2024.

records.limitations: F denotes an actual coarse-grained elastic-network vibration calculation, not quantum-chemical molecular frequencies or ideal-gas thermochemistry. No D mark: MD is mentioned as an extensible capability and used in training another predictor, rather than demonstrated as an agent-run dynamics task.

records.name: NAMD-Agent
records.demonstrated_target: proteins in explicit solvent and lipid membranes, including 1UBQ, 1L2Y and membrane-builder examples
records.boundary_conditions: Explicit periodic boundary conditions in the solution and membrane examples (SI §§6.1–6.6)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Gemini composes, executes and revises code to operate CHARMM-GUI, assemble solvated protein or membrane systems, run NAMD, and analyze actual 1 ns trajectories. Example simulation parameters explicitly enable periodic boundaries.

aliases: Automating MD simulations for Proteins using Large language Models: NAMD-Agent
records.limitations: The inspected evidence is v1. T and D are positively coded; control over minimization settings alone is not used to infer a separate demonstrated O task. Protein or membrane boxes remain in the soft/biomolecular class despite PBC.

records.name: ToPolyAgent
records.demonstrated_target: coarse-grained bead-spring linear, ring, brush, star and dendrimer polymers with solvent
records.boundary_conditions: Polymer–solvent simulation boxes are explicit; PBC is not separately resolved from the inspected article

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents invoke polymer/solvent construction and LAMMPS simulation tools. Brush and star examples execute dynamics, and interactive feedback changes grafting density or extends a simulation; research examples compare solvent interactions and polymer conformation.

sources.locator: Primary arXiv record and submission history
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The first report is dated 14 October 2025; the RSC journal title adds bead-spring but describes the same system.

aliases: ToPolyAgent: AI agents for coarse-grained bead-spring topological polymer simulations
records.limitations: Coarse-grained rather than all-atom MD. Interactive and autonomous modes are both included. The article HTML has a later rendering timestamp despite retaining the v1 identifier; date uses the primary submission record. Conformational/transport observables are coded under D, not F.

records.name: DynaMate (protein–ligand)
records.demonstrated_target: proteins and protein–ligand complexes, including BRD4 BD1 inhibitor MD and endpoint binding energies
records.boundary_conditions: Periodic boundary conditions with explicit TIP3P solvent and neutralizing ions (§4.3)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Planner/worker/analyzer agents build and parameterize solvated protein complexes, minimize geometry, execute GROMACS equilibration/production, and repair failed tool calls. BRD4 examples run 100 ns dynamics followed by MM/PBSA binding-energy analysis.

sources.locator: Title, author list and abstract of SimBioChem 2025 workshop counterpart
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The earlier workshop title DynAgent has the same five authors and planner/simulation/analyzer architecture. It is treated as the same system, not another agent. Exact public workshop posting date was not resolved.

aliases: DynAgent: A Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous Protein-Ligand Molecular Dynamics Simulations
records.limitations: The dated field uses the verified arXiv date; an earlier DynAgent workshop version is identified but its posting date is unresolved, so this is not a secure earliest-appearance claim. This is unrelated to the LAMMPS/Moltemplate DynaMate of de Gillis et al. Endpoint MM/PBSA analysis is included under D, without E/F marks.

records.name: MDAgent (biomolecular, 2026)
records.demonstrated_target: soluble and membrane proteins, protein–DNA/ligand systems and TMEM16F/XKR8 scramblase dynamics
records.boundary_conditions: Three-dimensional PBC for all simulated systems; explicit aqueous or lipid environments (Methods §4.5)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The LLM multi-agent system connects research planning to GROMACS system construction, steepest-descent minimization, equilibration and production. Demonstrations include membrane-protein dynamics and enhanced sampling; methods specify 3D periodic systems.

sources.locator: Primary record, title/authors and first submission
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The Ma/Yang/Song/Jiang biomolecular framework was first reported on 18 April 2026.

aliases: MDAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for End-to-End Molecular Dynamics Research
records.limitations: Distinct from the 2025 materials LAMMPS MDAgent. Umbrella-sampling PMF, metadynamics and SMD transport analyses remain D; no E/F/R mark is inferred from statistical free energies or transport paths. Some evaluation dimensions concern plans/reports, so task coding relies on the separately described executed simulation cases, not review scores.

records.name: Paimon
records.demonstrated_target: LiPF6 liquid electrolytes in DEC/DMC/PC and crystalline solid-electrolyte ion diffusion
records.boundary_conditions: Liquid cells explicitly require PBC in all three directions (§3.6); crystalline solid-electrolyte MD is separately demonstrated

sources.locator: §§2.1, 2.4–2.5; Fig.4 actual MD runs; Fig.5 solid-electrolyte example; Methods §§3.5–3.6
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Orchestrator/executor agents build electrolyte cells with PACKMOL, relax structures, run LAMMPS equilibration and production, and revise workflows using intermediate feedback. The article distinguishes 30 actual liquid-MD runs from gated tests with precomputed outputs, and separately demonstrates a crystalline solid-electrolyte MD workflow using LLaMP.

aliases: A Robust Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations
records.limitations: Cross-domain coding follows demonstrated liquid and solid examples, not general software support. Many repeated evaluations replace expensive dynamics with precomputed outputs; actual MD evidence is explicitly limited to the separate full runs and worked example. Transport coefficients are D, not F or electronic E.

records.name: CGMas
records.demonstrated_target: homopolymers and copolymers modeled with paired all-atom and coarse-grained force fields
records.boundary_conditions: Explicit cubic periodic cells and PBC in x, y and z (Methods §4.3)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM topology and mapping agents coordinate construction, review and self-correction. Tools build periodic polymer cells, minimize close contacts, execute atomistic annealing/equilibration, derive coarse-grained potentials from the trajectory, and run CG dynamics. PAN and autonomous polymer cases provide executed workflow evidence.

aliases: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics of Polymers
records.limitations: Human checkpoints are retained in the interactive route. Numerical stages use deterministic tools under LLM orchestration. Density, cooling-scan glass transitions and Boltzmann-inverted potentials do not establish vibrational thermochemistry; F remains blank.

screening.name: Polymer-Agent / PolyAgent
screening.locator: Methods, Table2/Summary of Tools; Workflow; Open Challenges and Future Work
screening.reason: The original report exposes generative/predictive model tools and RDKit validation for polymer SMILES discovery. It places integration of computational characterization and molecular dynamics in future work. No agent-executed atomistic simulation is demonstrated; arXiv:2601.16376 and DOI:10.1021/acs.jcim.6c00343 are counterparts of this same excluded system.

screening.name: AutoSolvateWeb
screening.reason: The original describes predefined intent/dialog flows collecting simulation keywords and triggering the automated backend. Generative LLM fallback only replies to unmatched/out-of-scope questions and redirects the conversation. Actual QM/MM/MD execution is demonstrated, but no LLM planning, computational tool selection, input modification or scientific feedback decision is shown. This is narrower than claiming no LLM is present.

screening.name: Large language models design sequence-defined macromolecules via evolutionary optimization
screening.locator: Main text introduction of optimizer; Methods/LLM prompts
screening.reason: The original explicitly takes a learned RNN approximation as ground truth and does not validate the full MD-to-morphology mapping in this work. LLM feedback distances come from that surrogate, not agent-invoked dynamics. Historical MD training data and MD-themed prompts do not establish an executed agentic atomistic workflow.

screening.name: DynAgent
screening.locator: Workshop title/author list and abstract; arXiv:2512.10034v1
screening.reason: Same Guilbert/Masschelein/Goumaz/Naida/Schwaller system as the biomolecular DynaMate. Name and evaluation-set size changed between reports; count once. Workshop posting date remains unresolved because the primary forum and metadata access returned challenge/403.

screening.name: DynaMate (de Gillis et al., LAMMPS)
screening.reason: A separate group and software stack use the DynaMate name for LAMMPS/Moltemplate molecular workflows. It must not be merged with Guilbert's protein–ligand framework. Primary screening and record are owned by the materials research file to prevent duplicate entries.

screening.name: Multi-agentic AI framework for end-to-end atomistic simulations / LAMMPS-Agents
screening.locator: Abstract and first-published metadata; Methods and worked elemental/alloy examples
screening.reason: Vriza/Kornu/Koneru/Chan/Sankaranarayanan framework (first published 9 December 2025) uses actual LAMMPS/Atomsk/Phonopy simulations. This is not either DynaMate. Demonstrated targets are elemental/alloy materials, and the materials researcher owns the record.

screening.name: Electrolyte agent (ICLR 2026, OpenReview MEXl18VhBL)
screening.locator: Indexed original PDF §§3.1 and 4; alternative original asset 837f62f17b0f4210dbc1260e813b7fd1ebabd467.pdf
screening.reason: Primary search results describe an MD-assistant and a discovery agent executing electrolyte simulations, potentially eligible. Direct PDF/forum reads encountered a verification challenge and metadata endpoint access failed; title/author identity, earliest date, full workflow and deduplication were not resolved. Do not add to the denominator from snippets alone.

screening.name: gromacs_smolagent
screening.reason: Official repository describes a Smolagents interface for GROMACS and a January 2026 presentation. A specific executed simulation example and first public project date were not independently established in this pass; retain as a lead rather than counting tool availability alone.

screening.name: OHMind MD Agent
screening.reason: Official docs describe polymer/ion-exchange membrane system building, GROMACS execution and transport analysis tools. A dated executed atomistic case and independent system identity/publication were not established in this pass.

screening.name: AIonopedia
screening.reason: Primary abstract presents an LLM-orchestrated multimodal property predictor, screening/design and wet-lab validation. No agent-executed atomistic calculation was established from the inspected evidence. Full-text confirmation is incomplete, so this is an adjacent unresolved candidate, not a definitive claim that the project lacks simulation capabilities.
